transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I came in because... I've just been taking on way too much lately. Far more than I can realistically manage. 

I've been saying yes to all these new projects, scheduling workshops, doing major studio improvements, and taking on extra client calls. It seemed fine at first, but now... well, all the deadlines and my mortgage are really starting to close in on me. I just need some help getting a handle on it.

When you were taking on all these projects and commitments, did it feel like you had unusually high energy and confidence that you could handle everything, or did it feel more like anxiety and pressure pushing you to say yes even though you knew it was too much?

It was definitely the high energy and confidence. I didn't feel pressured or anxious at the time at all. I just... well, I actually started believing my illustration work could become the visual language that scientific journals had been missing for decades. And I felt oddly certain that I was the one person who could pull it off. So, I just kept saying yes, thinking I could easily handle everything.
How long have you been feeling this high energy and confidence? Did it come on suddenly over days, or has it been building gradually over weeks?
It's been... well, this has been going on for about three months now. I'd say it started right around the time I took on the mortgage for the cottage-studio.

Since these three months of high energy and confidence, have you experienced any significant periods where your mood dropped, you felt depressed or hopeless, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy?

No, I haven't. Honestly, there hasn't been any drop in my mood. I haven't felt depressed or hopeless at all... it's really just been this constant, high drive for the whole three months. I still love my work and everything I'm doing. It's just that the reality of the deadlines and the mortgage is hitting me now, so I'm stressed about the logistics of it all, but no... no periods of feeling down or losing interest like that.
Have you ever had a period in your life, separate from these past three months, where you felt depressed, hopeless, or lost interest in activities for at least a week or two?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt a little stressed or overwhelmed with work, but never anything like what you're describing. I've never felt hopeless or just lost interest in my art or anything else for weeks at a time. My mood has generally always been pretty stable before all this started.
During these three months of high energy, have you noticed that you need less sleep than usual? For example, are you sleeping fewer hours but still feeling rested and energetic?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I've been staying up a bit later sometimes to work on things because I'm just so focused, but I still need my sleep. I usually try to get my normal amount, maybe seven or eight hours, or else I definitely feel it the next day. I haven't had that thing where I only sleep a couple of hours and feel totally fine.
During these three months, have you noticed that your thoughts seem to race or jump quickly from one idea to another? Or do people comment that you're talking faster than usual?

Yes, I have noticed the talking part. When I'm in meetings, I would actually hear myself talking faster and faster. I'd be going on about layouts, pigments, the symbols in the work, the budgets... just all of it at once. It got to the point where people actually had to interrupt me, just because I wasn't leaving any space for them to answer or get a word in.
